decisions.reason: As a niche geothermal extension of the tube business, it likely faces a tougher test against aspiration levels, but its strategic fit and the firm's slack make continued market presence slightly more likely than withdrawal.
This is a more standard geothermal offer that leverages existing tube and systems capabilities, so management would usually allow more time unless results clearly fell short of aspiration.
The surface-technology line supports the geothermal portfolio and uses the firm's materials know-how, though its several models make later pruning plausible if uptake stayed below target.
A fire-protection steel profile system is very close to the core building-systems business and likely benefits from regulation- and quality-driven demand, so continuation is likely.
The slim steel profile system is a close extension of the established profile business, so a large incumbent would normally retain it absent clear evidence of underperformance.

The decorative steel profile surface system is somewhat more discretionary than fire-protection products, but it still builds on core capabilities and can be supported within the broader solutions portfolio.
